summary: The screened August 10 arXiv window emphasizes heavy-quark transport systematics, quarkonium open-system algorithms, resonance sensitivity to the hadronic stage, magnetic-field spectral-function modeling, and physics-constrained AI/ML surrogates. The most actionable heavy-ion result is the laboratory-frame T-matrix correction to heavy-quark drag. The most transferable AI/ML result is the neural-operator plasma surrogate with residual and geometry validation. Two papers are flagged as caution: one uses ML in a generic collider-sensitivity study with unclear robustness, and one uses an overstrong quantum-computing title relative to the demonstrated finite-density QCD scale.
strongest_paper_summary: arXiv:2608.06731 is the strongest directly relevant heavy-ion paper: it removes a medium-frame ambiguity in nonperturbative T-matrix transport and reports 25-40% low-momentum heavy-quark drag corrections.

papers.title: Laboratory-frame T-matrix and heavy quark drag in the quark-gluon plasma
papers.abstract: The paper develops a laboratory-frame in-medium two-body T-matrix framework for heavy-light scattering in the QGP. It finds that center-of-mass-frame approximations can shift low-momentum heavy-quark drag coefficients by about 25-40%.

papers.title: Quantum simulation of bottomonium dynamics in the quark-gluon plasma via the Lindblad equation
papers.authors_short: Linyuan Wei, Jin Hu, Anping Huang, Yunpeng Liu, Baoyi Chen
papers.abstract: The authors map an isotropic next-to-leading-order Lindblad equation for bottomonium in the QGP onto qubits and simulate Upsilon(1S) survival probability. They report a small final color-octet contribution and a circuit optimization requiring a single ancillary qubit.

papers.title: Reconstructability and directed flow of short-lived resonances in Au+Au collisions at 19.6 and 200 GeV
papers.authors_short: Junyi Han, Xialei Jiang, Hongcan Li, Yaping Wang
papers.abstract: Using UrQMD, the paper studies rho0, K*0, and Lambda(1520) reconstructability and directed flow in Au+Au at 19.6 and 200 GeV. It finds reconstructability is mainly controlled by resonance lifetime and that mid-central resonance flow can differ from stable-hadron flow.

papers.title: q qbar scattering phase shift in the pi0 channel and pi0 meson spectral function under external magnetic field and finite meson momentum
papers.authors_short: Min Zhou, Zhiyang Liu, Yvming Tian, Chonglong Xie, Guoyun Shao, Shijun Mao
papers.abstract: The paper computes pi0-channel q qbar phase shifts and spectral functions in a two-flavor NJL model under external magnetic field and finite meson momentum. It identifies bound, resonant, and non-Breit-Wigner structures and magnetic-field-induced anisotropy.

papers.title: Extraction of Pion Unpolarized Quark and Gluon Generalized Parton Distributions using Deep Neural-Networks
papers.authors_short: Satyajit Puhan, Shubham Sharma, Narinder Kumar
papers.abstract: The authors use a physics-informed neural-network parameterization to extract pion quark and gluon GPDs from JAM21/xFitter PDFs, pion electromagnetic form-factor data, gravitational form-factor constraints, and lattice-QCD results. PDF replica ensembles provide uncertainty bands.

papers.title: Millisecond-Scale Neural Operator Surrogates for Double-Null Free-Boundary Grad-Shafranov Equilibria
papers.abstract: A geometrically conditioned Fourier Neural Operator is trained on FreeGS double-null equilibrium solutions and reaches 0.05% mean relative L2 error, X-point recovery within 0.2 cm, FreeGS-level residual diagnostics, and millisecond evaluation latency.

papers.title: Unsupervised Adaptation of PDE Foundation Models
papers.authors_short: Ziye Song, Zhao Wei, Xin Yu, Ivor Tsang, Yueming Lyu
papers.abstract: The paper pretrains a neighborhood-attention Transformer on diverse PDEs and adapts it to unseen PDEs without ground-truth solutions, using PDE residuals, boundary conditions, LoRA, and a Newton-Schulz orthogonalized variant.

papers.title: Alternating Levenberg-Marquardt Training of Physics-Informed Neural Networks with Fourier-Enhanced Features
papers.authors_short: Yulun Wu, Matthieu Barreau, Miguel Aguiar, Karl H. Johansson
papers.abstract: FALM-PINN decouples Fourier-enhanced representation learning from coefficient fitting using a lower-level Levenberg-Marquardt nonlinear least-squares solve. The paper reports up to two orders of magnitude lower relative L2 error on high-frequency and nonlinear PDE benchmarks.

cautions.title: Probing dark matter through charged Higgs pair production at future multi-TeV muon colliders: A machine-learning analysis
cautions.authors_short: Khiem Hong Phan, Quang Hoang-Minh Pham
cautions.abstract: The paper studies Inert Doublet Model charged-Higgs pair production at future muon colliders and reports that ML improves signal sensitivity over cut-based selections for several benchmark points.
cautions.reason: This is a plausible collider-phenomenology exercise, but the abstract presents ML mainly as a sensitivity enhancer without enough visible information about robustness, systematic uncertainties, or transferability. It should not be treated as a strong physics-AI contribution from the abstract alone.

cautions.title: Quantum Computers will constrain the Equation of State of Neutron Stars
cautions.authors_short: Adrian Castano-Garcia, Nahia J. Dios-Bilbao, J. J. Galvez-Viruet, Felipe J. Llanes-Estrada, Mario Logrosan-Alvarez, Nicolas M. Arenaza, Maria Gomez-Rocha
cautions.abstract: The paper frames future quantum computers as a route to finite-density QCD and neutron-star EoS constraints, develops canonical Hamiltonian ingredients, and demonstrates finite-chemical-potential QCD for a few particles and momentum modes on a classical cluster.
cautions.reason: The long-term motivation is legitimate, but the title overstates present capability. A three-to-four-particle demonstration is far from constraining neutron-star observables, so this should be read as algorithmic groundwork rather than a near-term EoS result.
